query: What is the current status of SpaceX Starship Flight 13 (IFT-13) as of mid-July 2026? Has Booster 20 completed its static fire test? Has the FAA approved Flight 13 / accepted the Flight 12 mishap investigation? What is the latest NET (no earlier than) launch date shown on trackers like NextSpaceflight and RGV Aerial Photography?
answer:
I've completed my research on SpaceX Starship Flight 13 (IFT-13). Here's the bottom-line summary:

**Booster 20 static fire:** ✅ Completed — full 33-engine static fire on July 10, 2026 (longest Super Heavy static fire to date). Ship 40 completed a 60-second static fire July 1.

**FAA approval / Flight 12 mishap investigation:** ✅ Cleared — the FAA closed the Flight 12 mishap investigation, accepted SpaceX's findings and corrective actions, and cleared Flight 13 to launch (no public injuries/property damage from Flight 12). This reversed the FAA's May 27 requirement for an investigation before resuming flights.

**Launch status:** ❌ The July 16, 2026 attempt was **aborted automatically at T-0** when ~4 of the 33 Raptor 3 booster engines failed to ignite. Musk said 2 Raptors will be swapped, with "most probable launch timing early next week."

**Latest NET on trackers:** NextSpaceflight shows **Monday, July 20, 2026 at 22:45 GMT**. Other trackers (RocketLaunch.Live, WhatAboutIt) still listed generic "July 2026" at access time. SpaceX had not issued a final official new-date confirmation as of July 17.

key_facts: Flight 13 uses Booster 20 (Super Heavy V3) and Ship 40; it is the second flight of the V3 generation.
Booster 20 completed a full 33-engine static fire (~25 seconds) on July 10, 2026 - the longest Super Heavy static fire to date.
Ship 40 completed a 60-second static fire on July 1, 2026, plus cryo proof tests (May 4-5) and a 6-engine checkout.
The FAA closed its Flight 12 mishap investigation, accepted SpaceX's findings/corrective actions, and cleared Flight 13 for launch (no public injuries or property damage from Flight 12).
This reversed the FAA's May 27, 2026 requirement for a SpaceX-led mishap investigation before resuming launches.
The July 16, 2026 launch attempt (2245 GMT, Pad 2, Starbase TX) was aborted automatically at T-0 when Raptor 3 engines failed to ignite (~4 of 33 booster engines).
Elon Musk said 2 Raptors will be removed and replaced, with 'most probable launch timing early next week.'
NextSpaceflight lists the current NET as Monday, July 20, 2026 at 22:45 GMT (window close 00:15 GMT).
As of July 17, 2026, SpaceX had not issued a final official confirmation of the new launch date; some trackers still showed generic 'July 2026.'

Mission objectives: deploy 20 Starlink V3 satellites (6 with heat-shield cameras), booster boostback/landing burn offshore in the Gulf, and Ship in-space Raptor relight with Indian Ocean splashdown; potentially the final suborbital Starship test flight.
